FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides 
Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Divisional Council. 


Fipronil technical is used in the preparation of insecticidal formulations for environmental/agricultural/health 
purpose uses. 


Fipronil is the accepted common name by the international organization for standardization for 5-Amino-1-[2,6- 
dichloro-4-(trifluoromethyl)phenyl]-4-[(trifluoromethyl)sulfinyl]-IH-pyrazole-3-cabonitrile. 


The empirical and structural formulae and the molecular mass of fipronil are given below: 


Empirical Formula Structural Formula Molecular Mass 
CN 
N 
C12H4CLF6N4OS FSC | 437.14 
S=0 
CI HN kas 


In the preparation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Insecticide Act, 1968, 
and the rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the Insecticides 
Act and rules, wherever applicable. 


The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex B. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with 
IS 2 : 2022 ‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (second revision)’. The number of significant places retained 
in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 18389 : 2023 


Indian Standard 


FIPRONIL, TECHNICAL — SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements and the 
methods of sampling and test for fipronil, technical. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards given below contain provisions which 
through reference in this text, constituteprovisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent edition of these 
standards: 


IS No. Title 
IS 1070 : 2023 Reagent grade water — 
Specification (fourth 
revision)

technical grade pesticides 
(first revision) 


3 REQUIREMENTS 


3.1 Description 


The material shall be in the form of white to beige 
coloured lumps or powder with characteristic smell. 
It shall be devoid of hard aggregates and free of 
extraneous matter. 


3.2 The material shall also comply with the 
requirements given in Table 1. 


4 PACKING 


The material shall be packed in LDPE/HDPE sack of 
thickness not less than 0.125 mm. The capacity of the 
LDPE/HDPE sack shall be 25 kg, 50 kg, and 100 kg. 
This shall be individually packed in fiber board drum 


with metal on the base and the lid. The capacity of the 
fiber board drum shall be 25 kg, 50 kg, and 100 kg 
only. The container shall also meet the general 
requirements given in 8190 (Part 1). 


5 MARKING 


5.1 The sack shall bear legibly and indelibly the 
following: 


a) Name of the material; 

b) Name and address of the manufacturer; 

c) Batch number; 

d) Date of manufacture; 

e) Date of expiry; 

f) Net quantity; 

g) Nominal Fipronil content, percent (m/m); 

h) Cautionary notice as worded in the 
Insecticides Act, 1968, and rules framed 
thereunder; and 

j) Any other information required under the 
(Legal Metrology Packaged Commodities) 
Rules, 2011. 


5.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product(s) conforming to the requirements of this 
standard may be certified as per the conformity 
assessment schemes under the provisions of the 
Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016 and the 
Rules and Regulations framed thereunder, and the 
products may be marked with the Standard Mark. 


6 SAMPLING 


Representative samples of the material shall be drawn 
as prescribed in IS 10946. 


7 TESTS 


7.1 Tests shall be carried out by the methods referred 
to in col (4) of Table 1. 


7.2 Quality of Reagents 
Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and 
reagent grade water (see IS 1070) shall be employed 


in the tests. 


NOTE — 'Pure chemicals' shall mean chemicals that do 
not contain impurities which affect the results of analysis.

ANNEX A 
[Table 1, SI No. (i)] 


DETERMINATION OF FIPRONIL CONTENT 


A-1 PRINCIPLE 


The fipronil content is determined by high 
performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) 
equipped with UV-VIS detector using internal 
standard technique. 


A-2 APPARATUS 


A-2.1 A high performance liquid chromatography 
system equipped with ultraviolet detector and 
chromatographic  software/printer  plotter-cum- 
integrator is used for this determination. The 
suggested operative parameters are as follows, but can 
be changed, if necessary, provided standardization is 
done: 


Column Stainless steel, 
25 cm x 4.61 mm i.d., 
packed with 5 um 
Cosmosil packed, RP 18 


Temperature Ambient 

Mobile phase Acetonitrile : Water 
(80 : 20 v/v) 

Flow rate 0.5 ml/min 

Injection volume 20 ul 

Detector Ultraviolet detector 
(280 nm) 


A typical HPLC chromatograms of fipronil, technical 
are given in Fig. 1 and Fig. 2. 


A-2.2 Analytical Balance 

A-2.3 Microlitre Syringe — 25 ul capacity 
A-2.4 Magnetic Stirrer 

A-2.5 Ultrasonic Bath 

A-2.6 Standard Glassware 

A-3 REAGENTS 


A-3.1 Fipronil Reference Standard — of known 
purity 


A-3.2 Acetonitrile — HPLC/AR grade 


A-3.3 Water — HPLC/AR grade 


A-3.4 Acetophenone (Internal Standard) — of 
known purity 


A-4 PROCEDURE 


A-4.1 Preparation of Mobile Phase 


Mix acetonitrile and water in the proportion of 
80 : 20 vv and pass through membrane filter under 
vacuum. Homogenize the mixture using a magnetic 
stirrer and allow to attain room temperature. 


NOTE — Dissolution of acetonitrile in water is endothermic, 
hence allow the mixing to start at ambienttemperature and 
continue till it attains room temperature. 


A-4.2 Preparation of Internal Standard Solution 


Weigh accurately 0.1 g acetophenone (99.0 percent) 
into a 25 ml (Concentration 4 mg per ml) volumetric 
flask. Dissolve this in acetonitrile and ultrasonicate for 
10 minutes. Make up to volume with acetonitrile. 


A-4.3 Preparation of Standard Solution 


Weigh accurately 0.1 g of fipronil analytical standard 
of known purity into 100 ml volumetric flask. Add 
50 ml of acetonitrile and dissolve content manually by 
shaking and sonicate for 15 minutes. Allow it to attain 
room temperature and make up the volume up to the 
mark with acetonitrile. Call this as Solution “A”. 
(conc. 1 mg per ml) 


Pipette out 10 ml solution “A” into a 100 ml 
volumetric flask and make up the volume upto the 
mark with acetonitrile. Shake well to homogenize. 
Call this as Solution “B”. 


Pipette out 5.0 ml of Solution “B” into a 50 ml 
volumetric flask and add 5 ml Internal Standard 
solution by pipette and make up the volume upto 
the mark with mobile phase and homogenize. Call this 
as Solution “C”. 


A-4.4 Preparation of Sample Solution 


Weigh accurately 0.1 g of previously dried (for 4 h at 
105 *C) fipronil technical into a 100 ml volumetric 
flask and proceed as in A-4.3. 


A-5 ESTIMATION 


5.1 Inject 20 ul standard solutions until the area 
quotients of reference standard solution/ sample 
solution of two successive chromatograms do not 
deviate from each other by more than 2 percent.

Review of Indian Standards 


Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the website- 
www.bis.gov.in or www.standardsbis.in.
